To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the accumulation of intracelluar fatty acid-derived metabolitessuch as diacylglycerols, fatty acyl-CoA, and ceramides, causes insulin resistance by impairing insulin signaling in muscle and liver, independent of circulating hormones.
overexpression of lipase in either muscle or liver causes tissue-specific insulin-resistant states, which are associated with increases in fatty acid-derived metabolite levels.

tissue-specific overexpression of LPL in muscle and liver causes tissue-specific insulin sensitivity, and that the mechanism of this insulin resistance involves the accumulation of intracytoplasmic fatty acid-derived metabolite(s) in muscle and liver, which impair insulin action and signaling via alterations in the PI3-kinase signaling pathway.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms of insulin resistance and the role of lipoprotein metabolism in this process.
the role of tissue-specific lipoprotein lipases in regulating fat metabolism and the development of tissue-specific insulin resistance and type 2 diabetes.
the mechanisms by which fat accumulation causes insulin resistance in skeletal muscle (muscle–lipoprotein mice) and liver (liver–lipoprotein transgenic mice).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the accumulation of intramuscular and intraliver triglycerides is a direct consequence of increased lipoprotein lipolysis in muscle and liver, respectively, and this is the primary mechanism by which insulin signaling is impaired in these tissues.

tissue-specific overexpression of LPL causes tissue-specific insulin action and signaling defects and that these defects are associated with increases in fatty acyl CoAs, diacylglycerols, and ceramides.
tissue-specific overexpression of the lipoprotein lipas gene results in a tissue-specific accumulation of fatty acyl CoAs, which is associated with insulin resistance.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

tissue-specific overexpression of LPL causes tissue-specific insulin action and that this insulin action is mediated via alterations in fatty acid metabolism and the insulin signaling cascade, independent of circulating hormones.
tissue-specific increase in fatty acid metabolism causes insulin resistance in skeletal muscle or liver by altering insulin signaling.
the overexpression of lipase in skeletal muscle and the liver causes insulin resistance, which is associated with an increase in intracellular fatty acyl metabolites.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the accumulation of fat within a cell is associated with insulin resistance and that this effect is tissue-specific.
insulin resistance in the skeletal muscle and liver can result from the accumulation of fatty acid-derived metabolite, independent of circulating hormones.
insulin resistance is not a generalized condition but a tissue-specific condition, with the liver being more sensitive than muscle to the development of insulin resistance.
